near_misses.what: The F1 helper realize.search(tries=1) always uses the fixed element order (t % 3 == 0 on its only try), so a Q-realizable matroid (C7-21) looked unrealizable. The search side only, and GP would not have been misled, but an agent could have spent effort on an EMPTY certificate that cannot exist (Singular would have said so).

notes: Pipeline: search/f2.py (untrusted: incremental point placement with per-point retry over Q and F_p[a]/(m)), f2_build.py (receipts in receipts/f2/, gp command list), f2_run.py (one gp call per line, refusals recorded verbatim), f2_empty.py (Singular sat/lift for entries with no Q point). Batch 1: 12 matroids (C3-01..C6-06), 25 claims plus src-F2^3, all held on first submit, 0 refusals. The search takes about 1 minute per matroid on one core, so it runs in 6 parallel workers. A gp submit takes 15-20 s at 60-75 claims, with the workers sharing the CPU. Singular: C8-62 and C8-67 (the F7 extensions) are EMPTY over Q with denominator 2.

Untrusted search over the 102 catalog entries not isomorphic to F1, in 6 workers, about 35 minutes of wall time. 100 have a Q point. Bad primes: 2 always, then 3, 5, 7. Points at those primes come from F_p, F_4, F_8, F_16, F_9 or F_25. Four entries have a Q point but no point in characteristic 2; Singular finds EMPTY mod 2 for each (C8-54, C8-61, C8-63, C8-65). Two have no Q point; Singular finds EMPTY over Q with denominator 2 (C8-62, C8-67), and they have points over F_4 and F_8. A structural check agrees: the first four are exactly the 8-element entries with an F7- restriction, and the last two exactly those with an F7 restriction.
